issues.issue: Sub-paragraph (5) covers additions under construction and materials "if not covered by other Insurance", a condition whose operation is left to be worked out, and the paragraph is interrupted by unreadable characters.

Item k. excludes property "covered under another coverage form of this or any other policy in which it is more specifically described", and "more specifically described" gives no workable test for which form governs.

The two caps interact awkwardly: (a) makes the Limit of Insurance the ceiling for loss plus debris removal, while (b) sets debris removal at 25% of "the sum of the deductible plus the amount that we pay", so the base of the percentage is not self-evident.

"[T]he increased costs incurred to comply with enforcement of an ordinance or law in the course of repair, rebuilding or replacement of damaged parts of that property" leaves open whether costs of rebuilding undamaged parts required by code are within it.

The coverage runs against Exclusion B.1.a, Ordinance Or Law (c149), which excludes increased costs of complying with an ordinance following a physical loss; the two are reconciled only by the partial carve-out in e.(8) (c070).
The paragraph is misnumbered "(7)" although e.(2) refers to it as e.(3), so the cross-reference chain in this Additional Coverage does not line up.
The paragraph opens with an orphan word "loss." carried over from the preceding text, and its (a)/(b) conditions are joined by "and", so whether both must be shown is left to construction.
This entry reproduces the whole of the prior-noncompliance paragraph (c066) verbatim before adding the pollutants/fungus exclusion, so the same words appear twice as separate operative paragraphs.

For a building insured under a blanket limit the cap turns on "the value of the damaged building as of the time of loss", and the form never says whether that value is actual cash value or replacement cost.
The blanket-limit formula has to be applied to the single $7,207,200 Blanket Building limit in the Declarations (c002), which does not allocate any per-building limit or value.

Payment is withheld "[u]ntil the property is actually repaired or replaced" and unless repairs are made "as soon as reasonably possible after the loss or damage, not to exceed two years", and "as soon as reasonably possible" supplies no measurable benchmark.

The clause disapplies the Ordinance or Law Exclusion only "to the extent that such Exclusion would conflict" with this Additional Coverage, a formula that itself requires a court to decide how far the conflict runs.
It is a partial override of Exclusion B.1.a, Ordinance Or Law (c149), and the two provisions cannot be applied together without deciding where one stops and the other begins.

It coordinates with the Loss Payment (c112), Valuation (c122) and Replacement Cost (c142) provisions, all of which likewise exclude ordinance-driven increased cost, so the boundary between those exclusions and this Additional Coverage must be drawn.
The trigger "[i]f a Coinsurance percentage of 80% or more or, a Value Reporting period symbol, is shown" is broken by a stray comma, obscuring whether both or either condition opens the Extensions.
It conditions coverage on the Causes Of Loss — Broad Form applying, but the Declarations show only the Special Form, so the paragraph has no field of operation in this policy.
The $250 per tree, shrub or plant sub-limit stated here is raised to $500 by the Kansas Changes endorsement (c257), so two different figures appear in the policy.

"[T]he applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations" for "any one occurrence" does not say how the single blanket limit is applied when one occurrence damages property at more than one described premises.
It has to be read with the Blanket Building entry in the Declarations (c002), which shows one limit across nine separately described premises.

The rule that losses to separate items "will not be combined" when "separate Limits of Insurance apply", coupled with "the Deductible will be applied only once per occurrence", does not resolve how the $5,000 deductible falls when nine buildings share one blanket limit.
The sequence here (reduce for coinsurance, then subtract the deductible) must be matched against the Coinsurance Condition's own Steps (3) and (4) (c126), which also subtract the deductible.
